New API types `PortfolioEconomicsStatusPositionRow`/`PortfolioEconomicsStatusExposureRow`/`PortfolioEconomicsStatusResponse` added to `api_types.rs`. Source chain, in order: (1) `st.execution_snapshot` for positions/cash (no broker call, no provider call); (2) `st.instrument_registry_path` v1 file -> `convert_v1_registry_to_v2` -> `validate_registry_v2` -> `bridge_instrument_registry_v2_to_economics` for the registry; (3) `mqk_db::fetch_recent_completed_bars_for_strategy` per non-flat symbol for marks; (4) per-position `value_position_economics` for every symbol that bridged successfully, or an explicit fail-closed manufactured `PositionEconomicsValue` (`InstrumentEconomicsTruthState::UnsupportedInstrument`) for a symbol absent from the registry or whose registry row failed to bridge — never a fabricated equity/USD default; (5) `aggregate_portfolio_economics` over the resulting position list plus `cash_micros`/a hardcoded `"USD"` `account_currency`. A new explicit `resolved: bool` field on the route-internal `PortfolioEconomicsPositionContext` (not on any pure 04A/04B/04C type) ensures the response's `quote_currency` is reported as an honestly-empty unknown for every manufactured/unresolved position, even though the underlying aggregator input carries `account_currency` as an internal classification-routing placeholder so `aggregate_portfolio_economics` buckets the position as `position_value_unavailable` (this route's real, specific reason survives) rather than the misleading `currency_conversion_unsupported`. Honesty flags `model_only`/`trading_uses_portfolio_economics`/`runtime_uses_portfolio_economics`/`risk_uses_portfolio_economics`/`order_path_uses_portfolio_economics` are hardcoded `true`/`false`/`false`/`false`/`false` on every response, including every failure envelope. `truth_state` vocabulary: `no_snapshot`, `registry_unavailable`, `registry_invalid`, `no_positions`, `active`, `position_value_unavailable`, `missing_marks` (route-level refinement of `position_value_unavailable` that fires only when *every* unvalued position's blocker is specifically a missing mark, never mixed with a registry failure), `db_unavailable` (overlay on `missing_marks` when `st.db` is `None`, mirroring `live-weights`' existing precedent), `currency_conversion_unsupported`, `nav_unavailable`, `aggregation_unavailable` (overflow).

**Equity active route proof:** a single `AAPL` position (qty=4, cash=0) against a seeded completed `md_bars` row ($25/share, real production registry) produces `truth_state="active"`, `nav_micros=100_000_000`, `gross_exposure_micros=100_000_000`, `net_exposure_micros=100_000_000`, `weight_bps=10000` (`ac04d_04`) — proving the full 04B-bridge -> 04A-valuation -> 04C-aggregation chain end-to-end against real DB marks. A flat (`qty=0`) position values to `active` with zero exposure without needing any mark (`ac04d_03`).

**Long/short gross/net proof:** `AAPL` long (+10sh@$20) and `MSFT` short (-5sh@$100) against $1,000 cash produce `nav_micros=700_000_000`, `gross_exposure_micros=700_000_000` (sum of absolutes), `net_exposure_micros=-300_000_000` (sign-preserving sum) — the long row's `notional_micros` is positive, the short row's is negative (`ac04d_05`).

**Missing mark / incomplete bar proof:** a non-flat `AAPL` position with the DB present but no completed bar at the queried timeframe reports `truth_state="missing_marks"`, with the row's `reason_code="missing_mark_for_non_flat_position"` and `mark_price_micros`/`notional_micros` both `null` — no fabricated mark or notional (`ac04d_06`). A bar seeded with `is_complete=false` is treated identically to no bar at all — confirming the incomplete row is never read as a mark (`ac04d_07`). The same missing-mark position with no DB pool configured at all reports the distinct `truth_state="db_unavailable"` (`ac04d_08`), mirroring `live-weights`' existing `db_unavailable`-vs-`missing_marks` distinction.

**Registry missing/invalid proof:** a registry path pointing at a nonexistent file returns `truth_state="registry_unavailable"`, HTTP 200, no panic (`ac04d_10`); a malformed (unparseable) registry file returns `truth_state="registry_invalid"` (`ac04d_11`).

**Symbol absent from registry proof:** a position held in a symbol the configured registry does not contain reports the whole-portfolio `truth_state="position_value_unavailable"`, with that row's `reason_code="symbol_not_found_in_registry"`, `asset_class=""`, `quote_currency=""`, and `notional_micros`/`absolute_notional_micros`/`weight_bps` all `null` — no fabricated equity multiplier, currency, or value of any kind (`ac04d_09`).

**Cross-currency unsupported — explicitly skipped, not implemented:** `convert_v1_registry_to_v2` only ever produces `Equity`/`Etf` v2 contracts from a v1 JSON registry file (confirmed by `ASSET-CORE-04B`'s own test-module docs for the identical limitation on futures/options/crypto/forex), so a registry row with a `quote_currency` diverging from the route's hardcoded `account_currency` is not constructible through a v1 fixture file without editing committed config, which this patch's hard safety rules forbid. The underlying `aggregate_portfolio_economics` currency-mismatch check itself is unmodified and already proven exhaustively by `ASSET-CORE-04C`'s own `fx01`/`fx02` tests (regression-verified unchanged by this patch, see below) — this route composes that check, it does not reimplement it.

**Filter/honesty/regression proof:** `?symbol=` filters `positions` rows case-insensitively without affecting `position_count`/`valued_position_count` (`ac04d_12`); `?limit=` truncates `positions` rows without affecting counts (`ac04d_13`); all five honesty flags are asserted identical across a `no_snapshot` response and an `active` response (`ac04d_14`); the real production registry with held `AAPL`/`MSFT` positions reports `non_equity_position_count=0` and `non_equity_enabled_count=0` (`ac04d_15`, the registry-wide count reused directly from the `ASSET-CORE-04B` bridge summary); `timeframe` echoes the query param and defaults to `"1D"` (`ac04d_16`); the route never mutates `st.execution_snapshot` (`ac04d_17`).

**Regression proof:** `routes/portfolio.rs`'s pre-existing `portfolio_live_weights` and every other handler in that file were not modified beyond additive new functions/imports — `scenario_portfolio_live_weights_01.rs` (8/8) passes byte-for-byte unchanged against the same real paper DB. `ASSET-CORE-04A`'s `scenario_portfolio_instrument_economics_asset_core_04a.rs` (31/31), `ASSET-CORE-04B`'s `scenario_instrument_economics_registry_bridge_asset_core_04b.rs` (18/18), and `ASSET-CORE-04C`'s `scenario_portfolio_economics_aggregation_asset_core_04c.rs` (21/21) all pass unchanged — none of their pure functions or types were touched. `scenario_route_contract_rt01.rs` (2/2) and `scenario_gui_daemon_contract_gate.rs` (23/23) — the GUI/route-contract regression suites most likely to catch an accidental shape or mounting change — pass unchanged; the new route is intentionally not added to the GUI probe manifest (no GUI consumer exists for it).

**Tests added:** `mqk-daemon/tests/scenario_portfolio_economics_status_asset_core_04d.rs` — 17 tests (`ac04d_01`-`ac04d_17`): no-snapshot/no-positions/flat-active (`01`-`03`), DB-backed active/long-short/missing-mark/incomplete-bar (`04`-`07`), no-DB `db_unavailable` (`08`), symbol-not-found fail-closed (`09`), registry missing/malformed (`10`-`11`), symbol/limit query filtering (`12`-`13`), honesty flags (`14`), real-registry non-equity-count proof (`15`), timeframe echo (`16`), read-only safety (`17`). DB-backed tests (`04`-`07`) were run against the live local `mqk-paper-postgres` container (port 5440, `miniquantdesk_paper`) rather than relying on the skip-without-`MQK_DATABASE_URL` path, so the active/long-short/missing-mark/incomplete-bar proofs are genuine DB-backed proofs, not skipped.

**Validation (all green):** `cargo test -p mqk-daemon --test scenario_portfolio_economics_status_asset_core_04d` 17/17 (run twice: once without `MQK_DATABASE_URL` — DB-backed cases skip gracefully — and once against `postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5440/miniquantdesk_paper`, all 17 genuinely exercised). `cargo test -p mqk-daemon --test scenario_portfolio_live_weights_01` 8/8 (regression, unchanged, DB-backed). `cargo test -p mqk-daemon --test scenario_instrument_economics_registry_bridge_asset_core_04b` 18/18 (regression, unchanged). `cargo test -p mqk-portfolio --test scenario_portfolio_economics_aggregation_asset_core_04c` 21/21 (regression, unchanged). `cargo test -p mqk-portfolio --test scenario_portfolio_instrument_economics_asset_core_04a` 31/31 (regression, unchanged). `cargo test -p mqk-daemon --test scenario_route_contract_rt01` 2/2 (regression, unchanged). `cargo test -p mqk-daemon --test scenario_gui_daemon_contract_gate` 23/23 (regression, unchanged). `cargo check -p mqk-daemon -p mqk-portfolio -p mqk-md` clean. `cargo clippy -p mqk-daemon --lib -- -D warnings` clean. `cargo clippy -p mqk-portfolio --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean (no `mqk-portfolio` files were touched by this patch). `cargo clippy -p mqk-daemon --test scenario_portfolio_economics_status_asset_core_04d -- -D warnings` clean. `rustfmt --check` on the four patch-owned files initially flagged formatting drift in all four (line-wrapping on long `use` blocks, closures, and multi-line `assert_eq!` calls); fixed via targeted `cargo fmt -p mqk-daemon -- <path>` on exactly those four file paths (not crate-wide `cargo fmt`), re-checked clean. No pre-existing drift encountered in any patch-owned file. The recurring `sqlx-postgres` future-incompatibility warning is pre-existing and unrelated.

**Safety confirmation:** no daemon runtime started; no provider/broker scripts or network calls; no live or paper order submitted; no DB mutation except isolated `md_bars` test-fixture rows scoped to dedicated test-only `(symbol, timeframe)` pairs (e.g. `AAPL`/`1D_AC04D_ACTIVE`), all inserted and deleted within their own tests, mirroring `PORTFOLIO-LIVE-WEIGHTS-01`'s existing `plw07`/`plw08` precedent; no DB migration; no strategy thresholds changed; no broker, OMS, risk, runtime, or DB schema code touched; no non-equity asset class enabled (route proves `non_equity_enabled_count: 0` for the real registry; the route has no enablement concept of its own); no live `PortfolioState` cutover; `.env.local` untouched; no smoke logs or generated evidence staged; `MiniQuantDesk_Master_Patch_Ledger_v2_updated.md` untouched/unstaged.

**Honest PARTIAL — `ASSET-CORE-04` remains far from closed:** this patch closes only the read-only operator status route gap. Remaining gaps, unchanged from `ASSET-CORE-04A`/`04B`/`04C`: no production portfolio-ledger cutover (`PortfolioState` is unchanged); no DB schema or migration; no runtime/orchestrator decision wiring (`mqk-runtime` never calls this route or any of the three models it composes); no broker/account sync; no real margin model; no currency conversion (by design — cross-currency positions are refused, not converted, and not even constructible through this route's v1-registry-only input); no non-equity asset class enabled; no real non-equity market-data source (still the blocking prerequisite `ASSET-CORE-04C` identified before any futures/options/crypto/forex math in this model could be exercised against real marks); and no risk/order path consuming this route's output (it has zero callers anywhere in the workspace, by design).

**Recommended next slice:** a real non-equity market-data source decision remains the single highest-leverage next step — without it, `ASSET-CORE-04A`/`04B`/`04C`/`04D`'s futures/options/crypto/forex math can only ever be proven against hand-built fixtures, never real marks. Absent that, the next safe off-market slice would be a GUI-side read-only consumer of this route (mirroring how the GUI already renders `/api/v1/system/instrument-economics/status`), which would need its own explicit scope/safety review before starting — this patch does not recommend or imply that as already authorized.

### ASSET-CORE-04E-NON-EQUITY-MARK-DATA-SOURCE-DECISION-01-COMBINED — CLOSED_LOCAL / PARTIAL

**Mission:** continue `ASSET-CORE-04` with the next safe off-market slice — a current-repo-grounded *decision* for the first real non-equity mark-data source/path that can eventually feed `ASSET-CORE-04A`/`04B`/`04C`/`04D` with real marks instead of hand-built fixtures. Not provider execution, not live market-data ingestion, not a production portfolio-ledger cutover, not live valuation cutover, not risk enforcement, not order routing, not broker integration, not a DB migration, not non-equity enablement.

**Repo evidence found:** `md_bars` (`core-rs/crates/mqk-db/migrations/0003_backtest_schema.sql`, unchanged in this respect through the current latest migration `0043`) has primary key `(symbol, timeframe, end_ts)` with `symbol` a bare unconstrained `text` column — no `instrument_id`, no `asset_class` column anywhere. Direct read of the full live mark-lookup chain (`ASSET-CORE-04D`'s `portfolio_economics_status`) confirmed it is symbol-string-keyed end-to-end: execution-snapshot `pos.symbol` → the `ASSET-CORE-04B` bridge keyed by `r.symbol` → `mqk_db::fetch_recent_completed_bars_for_strategy(pool, symbol, timeframe, 1)` → `select ... from md_bars where symbol = $1`. No charset/format constraint exists on `md_bars.symbol` (parameterized `sqlx::query(...).bind(symbol)`) and the existing CSV ingestion path (`mqk-md/src/ingest_csv.rs`) is equally symbol-format-agnostic, so a pair-style symbol like `"BTC/USD"` is storable today with zero schema change and no ambiguity against the current 88-row equity-only universe (no equity symbol contains `/`). `instrument_registry_v2.rs` (`ASSET-CORE-01B`) already defines validated, fixture-proven `ContractDefinitionV2::CryptoPair{base,quote}`/`Future{root,expiry,multiplier,tick_size_micros}`/`Option{underlying,expiry,strike_micros,right,multiplier}`/`ForexPair{base,quote}` shapes, fail-closed against `enabled=true` for any non-equity row outside a test-only escape hatch; a committed example fixture (`config/instruments/instruments_v2.backtest_suggestions.example.json`) already proves two disabled futures (`ES_TEST`/`MES_TEST`) and one disabled crypto pair (`BTCUSD_TEST`) with explicit economics metadata — no options or forex fixture exists anywhere. `config/providers/providers.json` declares broad `asset_classes` metadata for several providers, but only `twelvedata`/`alpaca` are `implementation_status: "implemented_equity_provider"`/`enabled: true`; the one crypto-scoped config (`coinlore`) is `candidate_unverified`/`enabled: false` with zero Rust implementation, and `TwelveDataHistoricalProvider`'s HTTP transport — while mechanically symbol-agnostic — has never been exercised against a non-equity symbol anywhere in the repo and is self-labeled equity-only. Direct read of `mqk-execution::asset_risk_policy` (commit `04a8fb50`) found `crypto_policy()` is the *only* non-equity policy with both `requires_margin_model: false` and `requires_contract_multiplier: false` — futures/options require both, forex requires a margin model — and crypto's two flagged requirements (`requires_session_profile`, `requires_currency_conversion`) are the lightest version among the four non-equity classes (24/7 needs no holiday calendar unlike futures' Globex sessions; a USD-quoted pair against a USD account passes `ASSET-CORE-04A`'s currency check trivially). `docs/audits/multi_asset_completion_audit.md` independently reached the same conclusion in three places (§1, §7-§9) before this patch existed, sequencing `CRYPTO-REGISTRY-01` → `CRYPTO-DATA-01` directly after `ASSET-CORE-04`'s foundation work.

**Decision made:** crypto spot marks (`BTC/USD`, `ETH/USD`), sourced first from a local, committed, no-network CSV fixture loaded through the existing `ingest_csv.rs` path into the existing (unmigrated) `md_bars` schema, behind a new but still-disabled registry-v2 entry. This combines the mission brief's candidate lane A (crypto spot) with candidate lane E (local CSV fixture-first) rather than choosing one in isolation. Futures, options, forex, and any live/network crypto provider are explicitly deferred (not rejected outright for the live-provider case) — see the decision doc §3/§5 for the full per-lane rationale. Recommended next implementation patch: `CRYPTO-DATA-01A-LOCAL-CSV-MARKS-01` (a sub-slice of the existing audit roadmap's `CRYPTO-DATA-01`, named in this repo's established `-01A`/`-01B` convention), scoped to one real disabled registry-v2 entry (closing `CRYPTO-REGISTRY-01` as a side effect) plus a committed local CSV fixture and a no-network proof that a real mark reaches the unmodified `ASSET-CORE-04A`/`04B`/`04C`/`04D` model chain for at least one crypto position.

No Rust source was touched in this patch, so `cargo build`/`cargo test`/`cargo clippy` were not run — there is nothing for them to validate.

### CRYPTO-DATA-01A-LOCAL-CSV-MARKS-01 — CLOSED_LOCAL / PARTIAL

**Mission:** implement the first safe, no-network crypto mark-data proof selected by `ASSET-CORE-04E-NON-EQUITY-MARK-DATA-SOURCE-DECISION-01-COMBINED` (§12 of the decision doc): add one real but disabled crypto registry-v2 entry and one deterministic local CSV fixture, then prove a real crypto mark reaches the existing `ASSET-CORE-04A`/`04B`/`04C` economics chain. Local CSV + disabled registry-v2 + test proof only — not provider execution, not live ingestion, not a ledger cutover, not risk/order/broker/runtime/DB-migration work, not crypto trading enablement.

**Repo evidence found (pre-flight, answering the mission's ten questions against HEAD `6b74c7b1`):** (1) a disabled crypto row validates today via `InstrumentDefinitionV2 { asset_class: "crypto", contract: Some(ContractDefinitionV2::CryptoPair{base,quote}), enabled: false, ... }` — no schema change needed. (2) `"BTC/USD"` was chosen over `"BTCUSD"`: the 04E decision doc explicitly named it, `md_bars.symbol`/registry-v2 `symbol` are both unconstrained text, the existing registry-v2 test helper `base_crypto()` and the committed `BTCUSD_TEST` fixture both already use slash-free *and* slash-bearing conventions interchangeably (no repo-wide rule either way), and the parser proof below confirms the slash survives intact. (3) The CSV fixture lives at `core-rs/crates/mqk-md/tests/fixtures/` — `mqk-md` had **zero** existing `tests/` directory (`Glob` returned no matches), so this patch creates that convention fresh rather than following one. (4)/(5) **Important finding the mission brief's own framing assumed away:** `core-rs/crates/mqk-md/src/ingest_csv.rs` already existed with 19 internal unit tests and the exact documented column contract (`symbol,timeframe,end_ts,open,high,low,close,volume,is_complete`, case-insensitive, decimal-string prices, `end_ts` as **integer epoch seconds**, `volume` as **integer**, not RFC3339/decimal) — but it was never declared as `mod ingest_csv` anywhere in `mqk-md/src/lib.rs`, so it was dead, uncompiled code; `cargo test -p mqk-md ingest_csv` would have matched zero tests before this patch. (The mission brief's own suggested CSV content used RFC3339 timestamps and a decimal volume, neither of which the real parser accepts — both would have silently zero-row-skipped against the actual parser contract, confirming the brief's example was illustrative, not copy-paste-accurate.) (6) `md_bars` read path is unaffected/untouched by this patch (no DB proof was needed — see below) but remains symbol-string-keyed per `ASSET-CORE-04E` §2 fact 6, confirmed unchanged. (7) Existing registry-v2 (`v2_01`, `v2_10`, `v2_17`, `ac04b_07`, etc.) and the new CSV tests below prove the parser/validator patterns. (8) `mqk_daemon::state::{instrument_v2_to_economics, bridge_instrument_registry_v2_to_economics}` (`ASSET-CORE-04B`) and `mqk_portfolio::{value_position_economics, aggregate_portfolio_economics}` (`ASSET-CORE-04A`/`04C`) are reused unmodified. (9)/(10) see "Built" and "Why no 04D route-level proof" below.

**Built:** (a) `config/instruments/instruments_v2.crypto_local_marks.example.json` — one real (non-`_TEST`) disabled registry-v2 entry: `instrument_id: "crypto:GLOBAL:BTCUSD"`, `symbol: "BTC/USD"`, `asset_class: "crypto"`, `contract: CryptoPair{base:"BTC",quote:"USD"}`, `currency`/`quote_currency` both `"USD"`, `provider_symbols: {"local_csv": "BTC/USD"}`, `enabled`/`paper_trading_enabled`/`live_trading_enabled` all `false`, `allow_enabled_non_equity_for_testing` absent (defaults `false`). (b) `core-rs/crates/mqk-md/tests/fixtures/crypto_btcusd_1d_local.csv` — 3 deterministic `BTC/USD` `1D` bars, real UTC-midnight epoch-second `end_ts` values (`1767312000`/`1767398400`/`1767484800`, verified via `date -u -d`), decimal-string OHLC with exactly 2 fractional digits, integer volume, `is_complete=true` on every row. (c) **`core-rs/crates/mqk-md/src/lib.rs`** — added the single line `pub mod ingest_csv;`. This is the smallest-possible fix for finding (4)/(5) above: zero changes to parsing logic itself, just registering the already-correct, already-tested module so it compiles and is reachable from any caller (including this patch's own new tests and, in principle, any future caller in or outside the crate). Chosen over writing a new parser (explicitly disallowed by the mission brief when an existing one suffices) and over routing through `mqk_db::ingest_csv_to_md_bars` (a separate, DB-backed, `csv`-crate-based ingestion path with no relationship to `mqk-md`'s parser — confirmed `mqk-db`'s `Cargo.toml` has no `mqk-md` dependency at all — which would have required a live Postgres connection this patch's safety rules disfavor when a pure in-memory path is available). (d) `core-rs/crates/mqk-md/tests/scenario_crypto_local_marks_registry_data_01a.rs` — 18 tests proving the registry-v2 fixture and CSV fixture independently. (e) `core-rs/crates/mqk-daemon/tests/scenario_crypto_portfolio_economics_local_marks_01a.rs` — 5 tests proving the full mark-to-model-chain.

**Registry-v2 proof:** loads via `load_instrument_registry_v2` (`reg01`); validates via `validate_registry_v2` (`reg02`); exactly one instrument, `BTC/USD` (`reg03`); `asset_class=="crypto"` (`reg04`); `contract == CryptoPair{base:"BTC",quote:"USD"}` (`reg05`); `enabled`/`paper_trading_enabled`/`live_trading_enabled` all `false` (`reg06`); `allow_enabled_non_equity_for_testing` is `false` (`reg07`); `provider_symbols.local_csv == "BTC/USD"` (`reg08`); `currency`/`quote_currency` both `"USD"` so `ASSET-CORE-04A`'s currency check passes with no FX needed (`reg09`); no future/option/forex row is introduced (`reg10`).

**CSV proof:** parses with zero errors via the now-wired `mqk_md::ingest_csv::parse_csv_file`, exactly 3 rows (`csv01`); every row's symbol is the exact string `"BTC/USD"` — the slash survives the parser unmodified (`csv02`); every row's timeframe is `"1D"` (`csv03`); every row is `is_complete==true` (`csv04`); row count and `end_ts` ordering are deterministic (`csv05`); the latest completed close is deterministically `"44100.00"` at `end_ts=1767484800` (`csv06`); decimal price strings and integer volume are preserved exactly, no floats (`csv07`).

**Mark-to-model-chain proof (pure in-memory, zero DB):** the registry-v2 fixture's `BTC/USD` row bridges via `bridge_instrument_registry_v2_to_economics` with `bridged_count==1`, `failed_count==0` (`chain01`); the bridged `InstrumentEconomics` carries `asset_class="crypto"`, `quote_currency="USD"`, `contract_multiplier_micros==MICROS_SCALE` (1.0x default, no explicit override needed), `model_only==true`, and `trading_enabled_by_bridge`/`enabled`/`paper_trading_enabled`/`live_trading_enabled` all `false` (`chain02`); the CSV's latest close (`$44,100.00`) feeds `value_position_economics` for a tiny `0.01 BTC` long position and returns `InstrumentEconomicsTruthState::Active` with `notional_micros == absolute_notional_micros == $441.00` (`0.01 * 44,100 * 1.0`) (`chain03`); that valued position feeds `aggregate_portfolio_economics` alongside `$100,000` cash and returns `PortfolioEconomicsTruthState::Active` with `nav_micros == $100,441.00`, `gross_exposure_micros == $441.00` (`chain04`), a `"crypto"` asset-class exposure row carrying the full `$441.00` notional and a positive `weight_bps` (`chain05`), and a `"USD"` currency exposure row with the same totals (`chain06`); every enablement-shaped field anywhere in the chain (`enabled`, `paper_trading_enabled`, `live_trading_enabled`, `trading_enabled_by_bridge`) is `false` for every row (`chain07`).

**Why no `ASSET-CORE-04D` route-level proof:** confirmed structurally impossible without touching forbidden files, not merely deferred by choice. `portfolio_economics_status` (`routes/portfolio.rs`) loads `st.instrument_registry_path` through `mqk_md::instrument_registry::load_instrument_registry` (the **v1** loader) and then `convert_v1_registry_to_v2`. Direct read of `convert_tracked_instrument_to_v2` confirms it unconditionally sets `contract: Some(if input.is_etf() { Etf } else { Equity })` and `quote_currency: None` for every row, regardless of the source `TrackedInstrument.asset_class` string value — so even a hypothetical `asset_class: "crypto"` row in `config/instruments/equities.json` would convert to a v2 row with an `Equity` contract, which `validate_contract_v2`'s `"crypto" => match contract { Some(CryptoPair{..}) => ..., _ => bail!(...) }` arm would then reject. There is no path for a real crypto position to reach this specific route today without either editing `convert_tracked_instrument_to_v2`/`instrument_registry.rs` (outside this patch's allowed `mqk-md/src` scope, which names only `ingest_csv.rs`/`instrument_registry_v2.rs`), editing the route itself (`mqk-daemon/src/routes/*` is forbidden), or adding a non-equity row to the live `config/instruments/equities.json` (explicitly forbidden and semantically wrong). This patch proves the model chain directly instead (above) and records that real route-level crypto proof awaits a registry-v2-shaped route-input seam — a future patch's decision, not this one's.

### ASSET-CORE-04F-PORTFOLIO-ECONOMICS-V2-REGISTRY-SEAM-01-COMBINED — CLOSED_LOCAL / PARTIAL

**Mission:** close the structural blocker `CRYPTO-DATA-01A`/`01B` (and `ASSET-CORE-04D`'s own closure note) repeatedly documented: `GET /api/v1/portfolio/economics/status` could only ever source its registry from the v1 file (`st.instrument_registry_path`) converted via `convert_v1_registry_to_v2`, which unconditionally stamps an `Equity`/`Etf` contract onto every row regardless of `asset_class`, so no real crypto/future/option/forex row could ever reach the route. Add the smallest safe, read-only, default-legacy registry-v2 input seam so the route can value the committed disabled `BTC/USD` registry-v2 fixture through the actual HTTP route via the existing `md_bars` mark path — without making registry-v2 the production default, without enabling crypto trading, and without changing broker/risk/order/runtime behavior.

**Repo evidence found:** direct read of `portfolio_economics_status` (`routes/portfolio.rs`) confirmed the exact pre-existing chain: `st.instrument_registry_path` -> `mqk_md::instrument_registry::load_instrument_registry` (v1) -> `mqk_md::instrument_registry_v2::convert_v1_registry_to_v2` -> `validate_registry_v2` -> `bridge_instrument_registry_v2_to_economics` (`ASSET-CORE-04B`) -> per-position `resolve_position_economics`/`value_position_economics` (`ASSET-CORE-04A`) -> `aggregate_portfolio_economics` (`ASSET-CORE-04C`). Critically, every step *after* registry resolution (`bridge_by_symbol`, `resolve_position_economics`, the aggregation/response-assembly code) is already generic over `&InstrumentRegistryV2` regardless of its origin — nothing downstream of registry load is v1-specific. This meant the entire structural blocker could be closed by adding an alternate registry *source* alone, with zero changes to bridging, valuation, or aggregation logic. `AppState` already carried a precedent for exactly this shape: `instrument_registry_v2_path: Option<String>` (`INSTRUMENT-REGISTRY-V2-SOURCE-01-COMBINED`), sourced only from `MQK_INSTRUMENT_REGISTRY_V2_PATH` and read only by the unrelated `GET /api/v1/backtests/economics-suggestion` route, including the exact load/exists-check/validate/fail-closed pattern (`routes/backtests.rs::backtest_economics_suggestion`) this patch's new registry-resolution helper mirrors. The committed `config/instruments/instruments_v2.crypto_local_marks.example.json` fixture (`CRYPTO-DATA-01A`) already carries a disabled `BTC/USD` `CryptoPair{base:"BTC",quote:"USD"}` row with matching `currency`/`quote_currency` (`"USD"`, so `ASSET-CORE-04A`'s currency check passes trivially); the existing `scenario_crypto_local_mark_db_persistence_01b.rs` already established the exact DB-backed-test seeding/readback/cleanup convention this patch's route-level test reuses. Direct read of `mqk_runtime::observability::PositionSnapshot` confirmed `net_qty: i64` is a whole-unit signed quantity with no fractional/micros representation — the route's `resolve_position_economics` already multiplies `net_qty` by `MICROS_SCALE` for every asset class, so this route structurally cannot represent the mission brief's illustrative `0.01 BTC` example without changing `mqk-runtime` (forbidden); this is recorded as a documented, justified deviation rather than silently substituted.

**Registry-source design:** new query param `registry_source` on `PortfolioEconomicsStatusParams` (`"legacy"` | `"v2"`, default `"legacy"` when omitted). New `AppState` field `portfolio_economics_registry_v2_path: Option<String>`, sourced only from `MQK_PORTFOLIO_ECONOMICS_REGISTRY_V2_PATH` — deliberately separate from `instrument_registry_v2_path` (which remains scoped to the backtests route only) so the two read-only routes' v2 configuration can never be accidentally conflated under one operator-set env var. No client-supplied filesystem path is ever accepted: the query param only *selects* between the legacy v1 path and the one server-configured v2 path; it never carries a path itself, closing the path-traversal/arbitrary-file-read concern by construction rather than by an allowlist. New pure helper `resolve_portfolio_economics_registry(registry_source, v1_registry_path, v2_configured_path) -> Result<(InstrumentRegistryV2, &'static str), (String, String)>` in `routes/portfolio.rs`: the `"legacy"` branch is byte-for-byte the route's pre-existing unconditional v1-load/convert/validate behavior, only moved into the helper; the `"v2"` branch loads/validates only `v2_configured_path` and never falls back to legacy on any failure. An unrecognized `registry_source` value fails closed before either branch runs (new `truth_state="invalid_registry_source"`, mirroring this route's existing always-200-with-explicit-envelope style rather than introducing an inconsistent `400` for one parameter).

**Response additive fields:** `registry_source_requested` (normalized request, or the verbatim invalid value), `registry_source_used` (`"legacy"`|`"v2"`|`"none"` — `"none"` whenever the requested lane was never loaded at all, proving no silent fallback), `registry_v2_configured` (server-side config presence, independent of what this call requested), `registry_v2_path` (echo of the configured path, never client-supplied), `registry_error_code` (`Some` mirroring `reason_code` only when the failure is specifically registry selection/load/validation, `None` for every position/mark/NAV-level outcome). All five are additive; no existing field was removed, renamed, or had its meaning changed. `registry_path`/`registry_v2_valid` keep their exact pre-existing meanings (always the v1 path; always whether the *registry actually used this call* validated, computed identically regardless of lane).

**Legacy/v1 proof:** omitted `registry_source` and explicit `registry_source=legacy` both produce `registry_source_used="legacy"` with `truth_state`/`nav_micros`/row shape identical to pre-existing `ASSET-CORE-04D` behavior, including when a v2 path is also configured server-side (proving configuration alone never changes default behavior) (`ac04f_01`/`ac04f_02`). The full pre-existing `scenario_portfolio_economics_status_asset_core_04d.rs` suite (17/17) and a same-file equity/legacy sanity re-check against a real DB-seeded `AAPL` bar (`ac04f_15`) both pass unchanged.

**V2 fail-closed proof:** `registry_source=v2` with no configured path reports `truth_state="registry_unavailable"`, `reason_code`/`registry_error_code="registry_v2_not_configured"`, `registry_source_used="none"` (`ac04f_03`); a configured-but-missing path reports the same `truth_state` with `reason_code="registry_v2_path_not_found"` (`ac04f_04`); a configured malformed (unparseable JSON) file reports `truth_state="registry_invalid"` with `reason_code` prefixed `registry_v2_load_failed:` (`ac04f_05`); a configured well-formed-but-invalid registry (unsupported `schema_version`) reports the same `truth_state` with `reason_code` prefixed `registry_v2_validation_failed:` (`ac04f_06`); an unrecognized `registry_source` value reports the new `truth_state="invalid_registry_source"` with the raw value echoed verbatim in `registry_source_requested`, never silently coerced (`ac04f_14`). Every case returns HTTP 200, no panic, and `registry_source_used="none"` — never a fallback to legacy while claiming v2 was used. The committed real `BTC/USD` fixture loads and validates successfully against an empty-positions snapshot with zero DB involvement, confirming `registry_source_used="v2"`/`registry_v2_valid=true`/`non_equity_enabled_count=0` (`ac04f_06b`).

### CRYPTO-DATA-01F-CSV-PROVIDER-METADATA-01-COMBINED — CLOSED_LOCAL / PARTIAL

**Mission:** close the provider-metadata/provenance gap `CRYPTO-DATA-01C`, `01D`, and `01E` each independently recorded: CSV-ingested `md_bars` rows carry `provider_id="unknown"` regardless of the CLI's `--source` value, because the CSV path calls the metadata-less DB helper instead of the existing metadata-aware sibling. This is provenance/evidence polish only — not a network provider patch, not a daemon route, not GUI work, not scheduler work, not a production registry-v2 cutover, not portfolio-ledger cutover, not risk enforcement, not order routing, not broker integration, not a DB migration, and not crypto trading enablement.

**Repo evidence found at HEAD `eaf82b7f`:** `mqk-cli::commands::md::md_ingest_csv` calls `mqk_db::md::ingest_csv_to_md_bars` (`crates/mqk-db/src/md.rs`), which parsed the CSV and then called the metadata-less `ingest_provider_bars_to_md_bars`, which always calls the inner helper with `MdBarProviderMetadata::unknown()` — the exact, sole root cause of `provider_id="unknown"` for every CSV-ingested row, confirmed by direct read (not inference). The metadata-aware sibling, `ingest_provider_bars_to_md_bars_with_provider_metadata(pool, args, provider_metadata: MdBarProviderMetadata)`, already exists and is already exercised by two other callers: `mqk-daemon/src/routes/ingest.rs` (live market-data-feed poll route) and `mqk-db/tests/scenario_md_ingest_provider.rs` (metadata-conflict-on-upsert test) — both confirm the helper's upsert SQL already writes `provider_id, provider_source, provider_symbol, ingest_mode, provider_bar_id, provider_updated_at_utc` columns that already exist in the `md_bars` schema (present since PATCH C's original migration; no new migration required, confirmed by direct read of the existing upsert `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` statement). `IngestCsvArgs.source` (the CLI's `--source` free-text field) was already threaded through to `MdQualityReport.source` (persisted in `md_quality_reports.stats_json`) but never to `MdBarProviderMetadata` — the two provenance paths had simply never been connected.

**Exact fix:** `ingest_csv_to_md_bars` (`crates/mqk-db/src/md.rs`) now builds a `MdBarProviderMetadata` from the operator-supplied `--source` label before calling the ingest helper, and calls `ingest_provider_bars_to_md_bars_with_provider_metadata` instead of the metadata-less wrapper. Metadata semantics: `provider_id` = `args.source` verbatim, or `"unknown"` only if the label is blank/whitespace-only (via the existing `MdBarProviderMetadata::provider_id_or_unknown` fail-closed helper — unchanged, reused as-is); `provider_source` = the same `--source` value; `ingest_mode` = the literal constant `"csv_import"` (a true mechanical fact about how the row was ingested, not a claim about data accuracy); `provider_symbol`/`provider_bar_id`/`provider_updated_at_utc` are left `None` — deliberately not fabricated, because `provider_symbol` is a single value the existing upsert SQL applies uniformly to every row in one ingest batch, and a CSV file ingested via `mqk-cli md ingest-csv` is not guaranteed to be single-symbol, so setting it from one row's symbol would misrepresent multi-symbol batches. `IngestProviderBarsArgs.source` (and therefore `MdQualityReport.source`/`md_quality_reports.stats_json`) is completely unchanged — still the operator's verbatim `--source` string, proving the quality-report provenance path this patch did not touch remains truthful and stable. No other function, route, or read path was touched: `ingest_provider_bars_to_md_bars` (the metadata-less wrapper) and `ingest_md_bars_csv` (an older, uncalled legacy function in the same file) are both untouched and still compile/behave identically — confirmed by the unchanged `scenario_md_ingest_provider.rs` 13/13 and the fact that `ingest_md_bars_csv` has zero callers anywhere in the workspace (grep-confirmed, out of scope, left alone). `mqk-cli`, `Import-LocalCryptoMarks.ps1`, and `Register-LocalCryptoIngestTask.ps1` required zero changes — the CLI already passed `--source` through to `IngestCsvArgs.source`; only the `mqk-db` internal wiring needed to change for the existing `--source` flag to become truthful provenance.

**Mission:** perform the first explicitly-authorized, read-only, bounded network verification of CoinLore as the crypto provider candidate `CRYPTO-DATA-01H` chose, continuing the crypto data lane after `CRYPTO-DATA-01A`-`01H`/`ASSET-CORE-04F`. Verification/evidence patch only — not provider implementation, not recurring ingestion, not scheduler execution, not DB ingestion, not DB mutation, not a production registry-v2 cutover, not portfolio-ledger cutover, not risk enforcement, not order routing, not broker integration, not a DB migration, and not crypto trading enablement.

**Repo evidence found at HEAD `4eaa14c2`:** direct read of `mqk-md/src/provider.rs` confirmed `RawBar`/`CanonicalBar` (aliased `ProviderBar`) require `symbol`, `timeframe`, `end_ts: i64`, `open`/`high`/`low`/`close` (decimal strings), `volume: i64`, `is_complete: bool` — unchanged from `01H`. Direct read of `mqk-md/src/provider_registry.rs::build_market_data_provider_from_config` reconfirmed exactly three factory match arms (`"fake"`/`"twelvedata"`/`"alpaca"`); `"coinlore"` still returns `ProviderFactoryError::UnsupportedProvider`, unchanged since `01C`/`01H`. Direct read of `config/providers/providers.json`'s `coinlore` entry reconfirmed `asset_classes: ["crypto"]`, `api_key_required: false`, `enabled: false`, `implementation_status: "candidate_unverified"`, unchanged. Pre-flight `git status`/`git log` confirmed branch `main`, HEAD `4eaa14c2` (the exact commit `01H` decided at), no dirty tracked files, only the expected untracked ledger-draft/smoke-log files present.

**Network verification performed:** 2 of the authorized 3 bounded, read-only, keyless HTTP GET requests to `api.coinlore.net` — (1) `GET https://api.coinlore.net/api/tickers/` (top-100-by-market-cap discovery/shape call, HTTP 200, 37,100 bytes, confirmed BTC `id="90"` and ETH `id="80"` present with `price_usd`/`volume24`/etc. fields, no per-ticker timestamp), and (2) `GET https://api.coinlore.net/api/ticker/?id=90,80` (targeted per-ID lookup, HTTP 200, 725 bytes, identical field shape for both symbols in one call). No credentials, no API key, no loop, no retry, no pagination, no backfill. No rate-limit headers were present on either response (`Cache-Control: no-store`, Cloudflare edge-cache headers only); this patch did not fetch CoinLore's docs page for official rate-limit guidance, recording that as an open item rather than assuming a number. Raw response bodies/headers were captured only to the session scratchpad (outside the repo), never staged.

**Finding:** CoinLore reliably identifies BTC and ETH and returns USD-denominated `price_usd` for both on two independent endpoints, but **neither verified endpoint exposes OHLCV history or any per-ticker timestamp** — only a rolling `volume24` (24h, not bar-period) and global-list-level (not per-ticker) `info.time`. Populating the existing `RawBar`/`ProviderBar` model as a completed bar from this data would require fabricating `open`/`high`/`low` (copying `close`) and fabricating `end_ts`/`is_complete` (asserting client-observed request time as a provider-confirmed bar close) — forbidden by this patch's authorization and `CLAUDE.md`'s no-fabricated-truth invariant. This data can honestly model a "latest mark" concept distinct from a completed bar, but not a bar itself without misrepresentation. Decision: **`PARTIAL_TICKER_ONLY`** (not `PROCEED_TO_01J` as originally scoped, not `BLOCKED_PROVIDER_UNFIT` — CoinLore is not rejected, its verified scope is narrower than `01H` assumed, and not `BLOCKED_MORE_REQUESTS_REQUIRED` — the verification completed within budget).

**Bounded network verification (3 of 6 authorized GET requests used):** 1 read-only fetch of Kraken's official OHLC endpoint documentation (`https://docs.kraken.com/api/docs/rest-api/get-ohlc-data`), confirming `security: []` (no auth), the exact 8-field response shape (`time`,`open`,`high`,`low`,`close`,`vwap`,`volume`,`count`), and the documented caveat "the last entry in the OHLC array is for the current, not-yet-committed timeframe." Then 2 live, keyless GETs: `https://api.kraken.com/0/public/OHLC?pair=XBTUSD&interval=1440` (200, 62 277 bytes, 2026-07-05T20:38:09Z) and `https://api.kraken.com/0/public/OHLC?pair=ETHUSD&interval=1440` (200, 61 855 bytes, 2026-07-05T20:38:21Z). Both resolved unambiguously (`XXBTZUSD`, `XETHZUSD`) and returned 721 real daily rows each. **Key finding, independently derived from the live response (not asserted from docs alone):** `result.last` is byte-identical to the second-to-last row's `time` in both responses, and the final array row sits exactly one interval (86 400s) later — a provider-supplied, mechanical signal for `is_complete = row.time <= result.last`, avoiding any fabrication. A second finding: Kraken's `time` field is the bar's **start**, not its end, so a future adapter must compute `end_ts = row.time + interval_seconds` to honestly populate `RawBar.end_ts`. Raw response bodies were written only to the session scratchpad directory outside the repo, not staged.

Default policy (`--no-update-existing` absent) sends every completed bar through the unchanged upsert helper (`sync_policy=upsert_existing_matches_ingest_helper_default_no_content_diff_skip_detection`; `rows_skipped_if_known=0` always). The optional `--no-update-existing` flag proves a real, provable-by-presence skip instead (`sync_policy=skip_existing_end_ts_no_update_content_diff_not_detected`): any completed bar whose `end_ts` was already covered is never sent to the write helper. Both policies are honestly documented as presence-based, not content-diff-based.

**Mission:** close two adjacent Kraken content-diff sync slices together — `CRYPTO-DATA-01AB-KRAKEN-MD-BARS-CONTENT-DIFF-HELPER-01`, `CRYPTO-DATA-01AC-KRAKEN-SYNC-CONTENT-DIFF-PROOF-01` — continuing after `CRYPTO-DATA-01Z-AA-KRAKEN-INCREMENTAL-SYNC-DB-PROOF-BUNDLE-01-COMBINED` (presence-based incremental sync; content-diff skip explicitly deferred). Add the smallest safe `mqk-db` read helper needed to compare existing `md_bars` rows for exact candidate keys, then update `kraken-ohlc-sync` so default sync truly skips unchanged rows, updates changed rows, inserts missing rows, and still excludes forming rows. Not recurring ingestion, not Scheduled Task registration, not daemon ingest job wiring, not GUI, not runtime trading, not crypto risk, not crypto paper execution, not strategy enablement, not production registry-v2 cutover.

**Pre-flight (run at HEAD `9cd2093a`):** branch `main`, HEAD at `9cd2093a`, no dirty tracked files, no staged files, only the pre-existing allowed untracked items (`MiniQuantDesk_Master_Patch_Ledger_v2_updated.md`, `smoke_logs/`). ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` with no content-comparison capability — exactly the gap `01Z-AA` documented as open, not an oversight.

**Answers to the mission's own pre-implementation questions:** (1) `01Z-AA` treated a new `mqk-db` read helper and/or a direct `sqlx` dependency in `mqk-cli/src/` as out of its own stated file scope; this bundle is exactly the follow-up that adds the helper. (2) `open_micros`/`high_micros`/`low_micros`/`close_micros`/`volume`/`is_complete` are sufficient to compare candidate `ProviderBar` content once the candidate's decimal strings are parsed via the existing (already-private, reused) `price_to_micros`. (3) `provider_id`/`provider_source`/`provider_symbol`/`ingest_mode` must be included so a row written by `kraken-ohlc-ingest` (`"provider_ingest"`) is correctly detected as changed when later touched by `kraken-ohlc-sync` (`"provider_sync"`), and so a mis-seeded `provider_symbol` is corrected rather than silently left. (4) Yes — a plain `select ... where symbol=$1 and timeframe=$2 and end_ts = any($3)` read needs no migration or schema change. (5) A map keyed by `end_ts` (`BTreeMap<i64, ExistingMdBarForProviderSync>`), since the CLI classifies one candidate bar at a time by its own `end_ts` and a map gives O(1) lookup without re-sorting a `Vec`. (6) No `sqlx` dependency was added to `mqk-cli` — the comparison logic (`price_to_micros` reuse) stays inside `mqk-db`, exposed as a pure `provider_bar_matches_existing` function that the CLI calls with borrowed references; `mqk-cli` never sees a `sqlx::Row`. (7) missing (no existing row) / changed (existing row, content differs) / unchanged (existing row, content identical) — computed once per candidate bar in a single loop before any write. (8) `--no-update-existing` is kept; it still refuses to write **any** existing row, but the evidence now distinguishes `rows_changed_skipped_due_to_no_update_existing` (withheld only because of the flag) from `rows_skipped_unchanged` (would have been skipped regardless). (9) DB proof needed: insert-missing, update-changed, true-skip-unchanged (no write-helper call), `--no-update-existing`'s changed-vs-unchanged distinction with the stale value surviving readback, true idempotency, forming-row exclusion, scaled-volume readback, metadata correction, `oms_outbox` isolation, zero-leftover cleanup — for both BTC/USD and ETH/USD. (10) `mqk-db/src/md.rs`, `mqk-cli/src/commands/md.rs`, the updated `01zaa` test, and one new dedicated `01abac` test file are sufficient — no `main.rs` CLI-arg change was needed since `--no-update-existing` already existed.

**Mission:** continuing after `CRYPTO-DATA-01AB-AC-KRAKEN-CONTENT-DIFF-SYNC-BUNDLE-01-COMBINED` (content-diff-aware `kraken-ohlc-sync`, committed `2f5d1840`), add a read-only daemon status route exposing Kraken OHLC ingest/sync evidence, mirroring the existing `CRYPTO-DATA-01N-O-P-LATEST-MARK-EVIDENCE-STATUS-BUNDLE-01-COMBINED` CoinLore latest-mark status pattern. Data/operator-visibility patch only — not a scheduler, not a daemon ingest job, not GUI, not runtime trading.

**Concretely:** direct inspection of `mqk-daemon/src/routes/transport_quality.rs::latest_mark_status` (the CoinLore sibling route) and its `LatestMarkStatusResponse`/`LatestMarkStatusRow` types in `api_types.rs` confirmed a reusable pattern: read `st.md_refresh_evidence_dir`, select the latest matching-prefix evidence file, verify `schema_version`, run fail-closed safety checks independent of the producer's own invariants, then surface `truth_state`. Kraken's evidence lane differs from CoinLore's in one structural way the new route had to handle: two distinct filename prefixes (`kraken_ohlc_ingest_*.json` from `01X-Y`, `kraken_ohlc_sync_*.json` from `01Z-AA`/`01AB-AC`) rather than one, and alphabetical filename ordering would misorder them (`"ingest"` sorts before `"sync"` regardless of which epoch is actually newer) — so the new route selects by the epoch-seconds timestamp embedded in each filename, not by string comparison.

**Built:**

Fail-closed safety checks: wrong `provider`, `network_call_made=true` without the `mode="network_smoke"` opt-in the CLI itself only ever pairs with a real network call, a `completed_bar_claim=true` field (Kraken evidence never sets this — presence is itself suspicious), `forming_candle_excluded=false`, `db_write=false` while `rows_inserted`/`rows_updated` > 0 (internally inconsistent), `md_bars_write=true` with `bars_excluded_forming=0` (inconsistent with the committed fixtures, which always carry one forming row), any of `volume_semantics`/`provider_id`/`provider_source`/`ingest_mode` missing, or any top-level trading/execution-like field (`order_id`, `broker_order_id`, `fill_price`, `position_id`, `account_id`, `side`, `limit_price`, `stop_price`) present. ### CRYPTO-REGISTRY-03-KRAKEN-DATA-ONLY-REGISTRY-READINESS-CLI-01 — CLOSED_LOCAL / PARTIAL

**Mission:** continuing after `CRYPTO-REGISTRY-02-KRAKEN-DATA-REGISTRY-CUTOVER-DECISION-01`
(decision-only, committed `4f157253`), add a read-only operator CLI/validator
surface proving the current, unmodified registry-v2 fixture and providers
config are ready for data-only Kraken OHLCV operations for `BTC/USD`/`ETH/USD`
— without touching any config flag, DB, or network call.

**Concretely:** `mqk-cli md crypto-registry-readiness` reads `--providers`
(default `config/providers/providers.json`) via the existing
`mqk_md::provider_registry::load_provider_registry`, and `--registry` via the
existing `mqk_md::instrument_registry_v2::load_instrument_registry_v2` — both
already-proven pure loaders, no new mqk-md code. It classifies: provider
existence, `provider_enabled` (an unexpected `enabled=true` fails closed as
`unsafe_provider_enabled`, per `CRYPTO-REGISTRY-02`'s decision not to permit
provider enablement yet), per-symbol `asset_class=="crypto"`, per-symbol
`kraken_pair`/`kraken_result_key` alias completeness (`missing_alias` if
either is absent), and per-symbol `paper_trading_enabled`/
`live_trading_enabled` (`unsafe_trading_enabled` if either is `true`). When
all checks pass and every requested symbol's `enabled` is `false` (the
current, correct state), the report classifies
`data_readiness_state=data_ready_manual_only` — explicitly not a failure and
distinct from `production_default`. `trading_readiness_state` is always
`"disabled"` and `scheduler_readiness_state` is always `"absent"` — this
command has no branch that could ever report otherwise, since neither a
trading path nor a scheduler exists in this repo to query.

**Built:**
- `core-rs/crates/mqk-cli/src/commands/md.rs` — new
  `CryptoRegistrySymbolCheck` struct and `md_crypto_registry_readiness`
  function (plus a small `fmt_opt_bool` stdout-formatting helper alongside

### CRYPTO-DATA-02A-KRAKEN-SCHEDULER-RATE-LIMIT-DECISION-01 — CLOSED_LOCAL / PARTIAL

**Mission:** continuing after `CRYPTO-REGISTRY-04-KRAKEN-DATA-ONLY-REGISTRY-STATUS-SURFACE-01`
(committed `49be663b`), verify Kraken's public rate limit against official
documentation and record a conservative, repo-local cadence policy for a
**future** Kraken scheduled sync — the gap `CRYPTO-REGISTRY-02`'s §7 and
`CRYPTO-DATA-01S-T` both left explicitly open. Decision/spec only. No
scheduler registered, no source code changed.

**Concretely:** performed exactly 2 bounded, keyless documentation-page
reads (zero calls to any Kraken **API** endpoint):
`docs.kraken.com/api/docs/guides/spot-rest-ratelimits` (authenticated-tier
call-counter system; does not cover public endpoints) and
`support.kraken.com/hc/en-us/articles/206548367-What-is-the-API-call-rate-limit`
(states public endpoints may be called at up to 1 request/second and remain
within limits; states OHLC/Trades are rate-limited by IP address **and**
currency pair, other public endpoints by IP only; states exceeding the
limit causes temporary throttling). Classified
`rate_limit_verification_status="verified"`. Recorded a conservative policy:
daily cadence, sequential-only pair calls (never concurrent), minimum 2
seconds between per-pair calls (2x the verified guideline), maximum 2 OHLC
calls per run (`BTC/USD` + `ETH/USD`), bounded exponential-backoff retries
(max 2, jitter, fail-closed once exhausted), and an explicit invariant list
a future task-registration patch must satisfy first.

### CRYPTO-DATA-02B-KRAKEN-SCHEDULER-READINESS-CLI-01 — CLOSED_LOCAL / PARTIAL

**Mission:** continuing after `CRYPTO-DATA-02A-KRAKEN-SCHEDULER-RATE-LIMIT-DECISION-01`
(committed `26a31cf3`), add a read-only operator CLI proving whether a
**future**, not-yet-authorized Kraken scheduled sync is currently allowed by
the `02A` policy, the current provider/registry config, and (optionally)
the latest Kraken OHLC evidence — without registering anything.

**Concretely:** `mqk md kraken-scheduler-readiness` deserializes
`--policy` (default: the `CRYPTO-DATA-02A` JSON artifact) into a typed
`KrakenSchedulerPolicy`, re-validates its own contract (schema version,
cadence/spacing bounds, concurrency, safety booleans) independent of the
PowerShell validator, and separately checks its
`scheduler_registration_status` field (`scheduler_already_registered` is
its own distinct truth state, not folded into `policy_invalid`). It reuses
the same two pure `mqk-md` loaders as `CRYPTO-REGISTRY-03`/`04`
(`provider_registry::load_provider_registry`,
`instrument_registry_v2::load_instrument_registry_v2`) to classify provider
enablement, per-symbol Kraken alias completeness, and trading-flag safety.
`--evidence-dir` is optional: when supplied, it finds the latest
`kraken_ohlc_ingest_*.json`/`kraken_ohlc_sync_*.json` file by embedded
epoch (same selection rule as `CRYPTO-DATA-01AD`'s status route) and
classifies it `safe`/`unsafe`/`missing`/`stale` — but only fails closed
(`evidence_unsafe`) when `--require-fresh-evidence` is explicitly passed;
otherwise unsafe/missing evidence is a warning only. `active`
(`scheduler_readiness_state=scheduler_ready_manual_registration_blocked`)
never means a scheduler is registered.

**Built:**
- `core-rs/crates/mqk-cli/src/commands/md.rs::md_kraken_scheduler_readiness`
  plus supporting types (`KrakenSchedulerPolicy`,
  `KrakenSchedulerPolicySafety`, `KrakenSchedulerSymbolCheck`,
  `validate_kraken_scheduler_policy_contract`,
  `find_latest_kraken_ohlc_evidence_file`).
- `core-rs/crates/mqk-cli/src/main.rs` — new `MdCmd::KrakenSchedulerReadiness`
  subcommand (`--policy`, `--registry`, `--providers`, `--provider`,

  macro invocation building this command's ~30-field evidence envelope

  compiler-macro-expansion limit only, not a runtime behavior change, and

### CRYPTO-DATA-03A-KRAKEN-SCHEDULED-NETWORK-GATE-01 — CLOSED_LOCAL / PARTIAL

**Mission:** continuing after `CRYPTO-DATA-02C-KRAKEN-SCHEDULER-READINESS-STATUS-SURFACE-01`
(committed `ad7b9aca`), add a second, explicit network opt-in env var to
`mqk md kraken-ohlc-sync`, distinct from the existing manual-smoke gate
`MQK_ALLOW_KRAKEN_NETWORK_SMOKE`, so a future, separately-authorized
Windows Scheduled Task (`CRYPTO-DATA-03B`, not built by this patch) can
authorize itself without depending on a variable named "SMOKE".

**Concretely:** `kraken-ohlc-sync` now accepts either
`MQK_ALLOW_KRAKEN_NETWORK_SMOKE=1` (unchanged, manual operator smoke) or
`MQK_ALLOW_KRAKEN_SCHEDULED_SYNC=1` (new) to authorize a live network
fetch when `--input-file` is absent; `kraken-ohlc-dry-run` and
`kraken-ohlc-ingest` are untouched and still read only the original
manual-smoke gate. The gate decision was extracted into a pure, I/O-free
function, `kraken_sync_network_gate(manual_smoke_env, scheduled_sync_env,
db_url_present) -> Result<&'static str, &'static str>`, in
`core-rs/crates/mqk-cli/src/commands/md.rs`, exhaustively unit-tested in
place. The command now also fails closed
(`kraken_sync_requires_database_url_for_network_mode`) when
`MQK_DATABASE_URL` is not configured, *before* attempting any network
call — a run that cannot persist its result must never spend a live
Kraken API call first. Evidence gained a new `network_authorization_mode`
field (`"input_file"` / `"manual_smoke_env"` / `"scheduled_sync_env"`),
printed to stdout and written into the evidence JSON.

**Built:**
- `core-rs/crates/mqk-cli/src/commands/md.rs` — new
  `ENV_ALLOW_KRAKEN_SCHEDULED_SYNC` constant, new pure
  `kraken_sync_network_gate` function plus its `#[cfg(test)]` unit-test
  module (`kraken_sync_network_gate_tests`, 4 tests), `md_kraken_ohlc_sync`
  updated to call it and to print/emit `network_authorization_mode`.
- `core-rs/crates/mqk-cli/src/main.rs` — doc-comment updates on
  `KrakenOhlcSync::input_file` only; no clap surface change (the new env
  var needs no new flag).
- `core-rs/crates/mqk-cli/tests/scenario_cli_kraken_scheduler_task_gate_03a.rs`
  — new: 1 negative-path subprocess test (neither env var set, names both
  gates), 1 `--input-file`-mode-unaffected subprocess test (using a
  deliberately-unreachable `MQK_DATABASE_URL` override so it fails on a
  connection error, never touching a real database), and 1 `#[ignore]`-gated
  DB-backed evidence-shape test following the existing explicit-`.env(...)`-
  override convention.
- `docs/runbooks/local_crypto_marks_ingest.md` — new "Kraken Scheduled-Sync
  Network Gate" section, including the `.env.local`/dotenvy caveat below.
- `docs/specs/crypto_data_02a_kraken_scheduler_rate_limit_decision.md` — no
  content change; re-validated against the existing guard, unaffected.
- `MiniQuantDesk_Master_Patch_Ledger_v2.md` — this entry.
- `docs/audits/multi_asset_completion_audit.md` — new closure note.

**Safety incident during development, disclosed honestly:** an earlier
version of `scenario_cli_kraken_scheduler_task_gate_03a.rs` tried to prove
"env var recognized" by removing `MQK_DATABASE_URL` from the test
subprocess's environment and expecting the new DB-url gate to trip. This
does not work in this repo: `mqk-cli`'s `main.rs` calls
`dotenvy::from_filename(".env.local")` at startup, which re-populates any
env var not already present in the child process from the repo's
`.env.local` file — so the removed `MQK_DATABASE_URL` came back as a real
paper-DB URL inside the spawned process, regardless of the test harness's
removal. Two of those tests then proceeded past the (correctly-passing)
opt-in gate and the (correctly-passing, because a real DB URL was now
present) DB-url gate, reached the live network-fetch call, and made a
genuine live call to Kraken's public OHLC endpoint for BTC/USD; a third
(`--input-file` mode) wrote real fetched-and-fixture data into the local
paper DB (`postgres://…@127.0.0.1:5440/miniquantdesk_paper`). This was
caught immediately from the tests' own unexpected-success failures (not
from silent success), disclosed to the operator before any further action,
and remediated with the operator's explicit go-ahead: `psql` confirmed 720
`provider_id='kraken'` rows for `BTC/USD` (none for `ETH/USD`, confirming
the incident's exact scope) and zero unexpected `oms_outbox` rows; all 720
were deleted and a re-query confirmed zero `provider_id='kraken'` rows
remain. The test file was then redesigned as described above (pure-function
unit tests for the "recognized" cases; the two subprocess tests kept are
both safe regardless of `.env.local`'s contents) specifically so this
failure mode cannot recur. No live order, broker, or trading path was
touched; the incident was confined to a public, keyless market-data GET
and a `md_bars` write for a symbol/provider this repo already treats as
disabled-by-default for trading.

mqk-cli --test scenario_cli_kraken_scheduler_task_gate_03a` — 2/2 non-
ignored pass, 1 correctly `#[ignore]`d. `cargo test -p mqk-cli --bin
mqk-cli kraken_sync_network_gate` — 4/4 unit tests pass. `cargo test -p
mqk-cli --test scenario_cli_kraken_ohlc_sync_db_01zaa` — 1/1 non-ignored
pass (unaffected). `cargo test -p mqk-cli --test
scenario_cli_kraken_ohlc_dry_run_01w` — 7/7 pass (unaffected; this command
was not touched). `cargo test -p mqk-cli --test
scenario_cli_kraken_scheduler_readiness_02b` — 12/12 pass (unaffected).
`cargo clippy -p mqk-cli -p mqk-md -p mqk-db --all-targets -- -D warnings`
— clean, zero warnings. `validate_crypto_data_02a_kraken_scheduler_decision.ps1`
— all 16 checks pass (unaffected; this patch changes no policy artifact).
`git diff --check` — clean. The `#[ignore]`-gated DB-backed evidence test
(`gate03_evidence_records_input_file_network_authorization_mode`) was
**not executed** during this validation pass, out of caution following the
incident above — it requires the operator to explicitly run it with

**Zero live Kraken API calls, zero DB mutation, and zero scheduler

### ASSET-CORE-01E-REGISTRY-V2-RATES-SCHEMA-GAP-01 — CLOSED_LOCAL

**Mission:** a session was asked to "start `ASSET-CORE-01`" via a three-phase

this patch traced the ledger's own "Recommended next slice" chain forward to
`HEAD` and found every open thread now blocked by hard session constraints
(live network calls, production cutover, trading enablement). A direct read
of the schema against the mission's own required-fields list (equities,
ETFs, crypto spot, futures, options, forex, rates/fixed income) found one
real, previously-unrecorded gap instead: `ContractDefinitionV2` had no
variant for rates/fixed income at all.

`ContractDefinitionV2` (`mqk-md/src/instrument_registry_v2.rs`) covered
`equity`/`etf`/`crypto`/`future`/`option`/`forex` — six of the seven asset
categories this schema is meant to represent per its own module docs and the
mission's own list. Rates/fixed income was absent from every enum, match
arm, and test fixture in the file; no committed patch across the entire
`ASSET-CORE-01`/`04` or `CRYPTO-DATA-01` lineage had ever added it.

`ContractDefinitionV2::Rate { issuer, maturity, coupon_bps,
face_value_micros }` (zero-coupon representable via `coupon_bps=0`; positive
`face_value_micros` required, following the repo's micros convention).
`validate_contract_v2` gained a `"rate"` match arm (non-empty
issuer/maturity, non-negative coupon, positive face value) — same
fail-closed shape-validation pattern as every other derivative class. Tests:
`base_rate` fixture; `rate` added to `v2_01` (mixed-registry parse/validate),
`v2_07` (missing-contract-entirely exhaustive check), `v2_17` (disabled-

roles — documented explicitly in the module so a future schema split

instrument_id/canonical-symbol (incl. case-normalized) failures, empty
symbol/instrument_id failures, BTC/USD fixture slash-symbol preservation +

symbol/instrument_id, and deterministic sorted-order rebuild proof.

### ASSET-CORE-05H-PURE-INSTRUMENT-SESSION-ROUTER-01 — CLOSED_LOCAL / MODEL-ONLY

**Mission:** implement `ASSET-CORE-05G`'s §7 safe closure target — close
the `"rate"` gap in the existing per-instrument session-profile resolver
and add one composed, reusable pure per-instrument session-routing
helper — without wiring it into any trading, admission, risk, broker, or
runtime path.

**Built:** `mqk-daemon/src/state/market_calendar.rs`:

- `resolve_session_profile_for_instrument_metadata` gained an explicit
  `"rate"` match arm — `SessionProfileResolutionTruth::UnsupportedAssetClass`,
  `profile: None`, reason `"rate/fixed-income instruments have no modeled
  session profile in this seam"` — so this schema-valid
  (`CANONICAL_ASSET_CLASSES_V2`) asset class is no longer misreported as
  `Unknown`/"unrecognized asset_class" alongside truly garbage strings.
  No new `MarketSessionProfile` variant was added — current repo defines
  no rate/fixed-income session shape, and inventing one was out of this
  patch's scope.
- `instrument_session_state_for_profile(profile, now_utc) -> (&str, &str)`
  relocated here verbatim (was a private fn in `routes/system.rs`,
  `ASSET-CORE-05B`) and made `pub fn`, so it can be reused instead of
  duplicated. `routes/system.rs`'s two existing call sites
  (`build_instrument_sessions_status_response`,
  `classify_instrument_session_parity_row`) now import it from
  `crate::state` instead of a local private copy — pure relocation, zero
  behavior change.
- New `route_instrument_session_for_metadata(asset_class,
  instrument_kind, now_utc) -> InstrumentSessionRoute` composes
  `resolve_session_profile_for_instrument_metadata` +
  `instrument_session_state_for_profile` into one pure, reusable,
  independently-testable entry point. `InstrumentSessionRoute` carries
  `profile_resolution`, `session_state`, `session_reason_code`, plus
  `is_production_backed()`/`is_model_only()` convenience methods mirroring
  the flags each route handler already computes inline. No DB, config,
  env, network, provider, broker, runtime, OMS, or risk access; no
  `enabled`/`paper_trading_enabled`/`live_trading_enabled` parameter —
  this seam has no enablement concept and the classification never reads
  or implies one. Not called by any route or production path in this
  patch (test-only consumer arrives in `ASSET-CORE-05I`).

**Deliberately not done:** existing route handlers'
(`system_instrument_sessions_status`, `system_instrument_sessions_parity`)
internal logic was left untouched beyond the mechanical import swap for
the relocated function — they were not rewired to call the new composed
`route_instrument_session_for_metadata` in this patch, to avoid risking a

rate/fixed-income was added. No `mqk-execution`/`mqk-runtime`/`mqk-risk`/
`mqk-portfolio`/`mqk-broker-*`/config/DB-migration/strategy file touched.
No non-equity trading enabled; no enablement flag changed.

documented profile, non-equity profiles are always model-only and never

— 11 pure `#[test]` functions (`ac05i_01`-`ac05i_11`), no DB pool, no
provider/broker call, no daemon/HTTP route, no runtime start:

- `ac05i_01`/`ac05i_02`/`ac05i_03`: equity and ETF route to
  `equity_us_regular`, `is_production_backed()`, and match real
  `NyseWeekdaysProvider::session_for` state exactly at regular-open,

  already proved against the real production calendar).
- `ac05i_04`-`ac05i_06`: crypto/future/futures/forex all route to their
  documented model-only profile, `is_model_only()` true,
  `is_production_backed()` false, at multiple timestamps (including a
  Saturday, proving forex's weekday/weekend split and crypto's
  always-continuous claim are exercised, not assumed).
- `ac05i_07`: option/options alias both resolve `profile: None`,
  `UnsupportedAssetClass`, and correctly report `is_model_only() ==
  false` (no profile to be model-only about).
- `ac05i_08`: `"rate"` resolves `UnsupportedAssetClass` (not `Unknown`),
  proving `ASSET-CORE-05H`'s fix.

  `mqk_md::instrument_registry_v2::CANONICAL_ASSET_CLASSES_V2` directly

### ASSET-CORE-02B-ORDER-INTENT-V2-SAFE-GAP-CLOSURE-01 — CLOSED_LOCAL / MODEL-COMPLETE

**Mission:** close the one concrete `ASSET-CORE-02` model gap identified by
`ASSET-CORE-02-03A-CURRENT-COMPLETION-AUDIT-01` — bracket/OCO representation
— as a pure, unwired model extension, without wiring `OrderIntentV2` into
live/paper trading or touching any broker/runtime/risk/OMS file.

**Built:** `core-rs/crates/mqk-execution/src/types.rs` gained
`BracketLegs { take_profit_limit_price_micros, stop_loss_stop_price_micros,
oco }`, a pure model of the common "bracket order" shape (parent fill
triggers a one-cancels-other take-profit/stop-loss pair). `OrderIntentV2`
gained an additive `bracket: Option<BracketLegs>` field defaulting to `None`
and a `with_bracket_legs()` builder. `validate_order_intent_v2()` now
validates bracket legs when present (requires at least one leg, requires
positive prices) and, when structurally valid, **always** reports
`IntentV2Routability::DisabledAssetClass` with reason code
`bracket_oco_model_only_not_executable` — regardless of asset class,
including equity — because no execution, OMS, or broker path in the repo
constructs or submits multi-leg/bracket/OCO orders today. `BracketLegs` is
re-exported from `mqk-execution/src/lib.rs`.

**Tests added:** `core-rs/crates/mqk-execution/tests/scenario_asset_core_02_order_intent_v2.rs`
(10 tests) covers: equity-without-bracket regression unchanged; equity with
both/only-take-profit/only-stop-loss valid legs all report
`DisabledAssetClass`/`bracket_oco_model_only_not_executable`; neither-leg-set
fails closed (`bracket_requires_at_least_one_leg`); non-positive take-profit
and negative stop-loss prices fail closed; crypto+bracket reports the
bracket-specific reason (proving bracket precedence over the generic
asset-class-disabled reason); invalid qty still fails closed first even with
valid bracket legs present; and the `BracketLegs`/builder field round-trip.

**Validation:** `cargo check -p mqk-schemas -p mqk-execution` clean.
`cargo test -p mqk-execution --test scenario_asset_core_02_order_intent_v2`

scenario_asset_class_guard_multi_asset_routing_guard_01 --features testkit`
— 8/8 passed (routing guard unaffected). `cargo clippy -p mqk-schemas -p
mqk-execution --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. `cargo test -p mqk-daemon
--test scenario_asset_class_scope_b8` — 12/12 passed (Gate 0 unaffected). CLI

### PAPER-SMOKE-FOLLOWUP-01C-WATCHLIST-V2-GATE-SINGLE-SYMBOL-FIX-01 — CLOSED_LOCAL / SCRIPT-ONLY

**Mission:** fix `scripts/windows/Start-PaperTradingSmoke.ps1` STEP 9B so it
classifies this repo's valid single-symbol `AAPL` paper setup truthfully
instead of falsely failing because no `watchlist-v2` artifact is configured.

intent: "a single-symbol artifact should use the existing single-symbol
smoke path unchanged" — STEP 9B had drifted from that design by gating
*every* invocation unconditionally.

**Built:** added `[switch]$MultiSymbolSmoke` (default off) to
`Start-PaperTradingSmoke.ps1`. STEP 9B now: (1) always fails closed on
`approved_for_live=true` (hard invariant, both modes); (2) when
`-MultiSymbolSmoke` is passed, enforces the original full watchlist-v2
preflight unchanged (`MULTI_SYMBOL_SMOKE_BLOCKED_SCHEMA_NOT_V2` /
`_NOT_MULTI_SYMBOL` / `_NOT_APPROVED_FOR_AUTONOMOUS_PAPER`); (3) when not
passed (default) and `watchlist/status.status == 'not_configured'`, reports
honest status (`watchlist_v2_status=not_configured_single_symbol_mode`,
`watchlist_v2_required=false`, `single_symbol_smoke_symbol=<symbol>`) and
proceeds; (4) when not passed and a watchlist-v2 artifact happens to be
configured and valid, proceeds with the single-symbol path unchanged and
says so; (5) when not passed and a watchlist-v2 artifact is configured but
invalid/unapproved, still fails closed
(`MULTI_SYMBOL_SMOKE_BLOCKED_WATCHLIST_V2_CONFIGURED_BUT_INVALID`) — a
broken artifact is a real misconfiguration regardless of mode, not silently
ignored. STEP 9B remains entirely read-only (no `Invoke-DaemonPost`); no
daemon readiness/session/risk/staleness/arm gate downstream is touched; no
`.env.local` write added.

## INTRADAY-PROVIDER-CLOCK-SKEW-OPERATOR-GUARD-01-COMBINED

### INTRADAY-PROVIDER-CLOCK-SKEW-01A-CURRENT-TRUTH-AUDIT-01 — CLOSED_LOCAL / DOCS-ONLY

**Mission:** grounded audit of the provider freshness/publish-lag gap exposed
by `PAPER-SMOKE-FOLLOWUP-01E` and `PAPER-TRADE-LIFECYCLE-PROOF-01B`, and a
safe patch plan for Phases B–D. Diagnostics/operator-guard only — no gate
weakening, no threshold changes, no forced orders, no live routing.

**Key finding:** `Refresh-IntradayMarketData.ps1`'s per-symbol
`latest_completed_bar_age_secs` is a snapshot computed once at
`produced_at_utc`, while `DATA-FRESHNESS-READINESS-GATE-01`'s dispatch-tick
check (`market_data_freshness.rs`) computes bar age live against wall-clock
`now()`. True bar age grows by the elapsed time between evidence production
and any later read — the exact mechanism behind the 2026-07-10 run's
900s-cap pass followed by a 913s-age fail 33 seconds later. Neither the
`GET /api/v1/market-data/intraday-refresh/status` route nor
`Start-PaperTradingSmoke.ps1 -RequireIntradayRefresh`'s `STEP 14C` currently
account for this: both report/accept `all_passed=true` at read time with no
visibility into how close the evidence already was to expiry.

**Built:** `docs/specs/intraday_provider_clock_skew_01a_current_truth_audit.md`
(full grounding: exact 913/900/2152 observed values, current evidence/route/
script field inventory, safe Phase B–D plan, non-goals) and
`scripts/guards/validate_intraday_provider_clock_skew_01a_audit.ps1` (static
text-presence validator, no network/DB/daemon calls).

**Validation:** validator PASS (all 10 required facts present). `git diff
--check` clean.

### INTRADAY-PROVIDER-CLOCK-SKEW-01B-REFRESH-EVIDENCE-LAG-CLASSIFIER-01 — CLOSED_LOCAL

**Mission:** add a pure, evidence-only freshness-headroom/overage classifier
to `GET /api/v1/market-data/intraday-refresh/status`, additive only, no gate
weakening, no provider/DB/network calls.

**Built:** `classify_proof_window_risk` (pure function, `transport_quality.rs`)
computes, from each symbol's already-parsed `latest_completed_bar_age_secs`/
`max_allowed_age_secs`/`passed` fields: `freshness_headroom_secs` (`Some`
only while still within cap), `staleness_overage_secs` (`Some` only once
past cap), `near_expiry` (`true` when still passing but within 120s of the
cap — `NEAR_EXPIRY_THRESHOLD_SECS`), `proof_window_risk`
(`"low"`/`"medium"`/`"high"`/`"unknown"`), and `operator_action` (present
whenever risk is elevated or evidence fields are missing). Wired additively
into `IntradayRefreshSymbolStatus` (6 new fields; all pre-existing fields
unchanged) via `parse_refresh_symbol`. A new `aggregate_proof_window_fields`
rolls the per-symbol classification up into three new top-level
`IntradayRefreshStatusResponse` fields: `proof_window_ready` (fail-closed —
`false` whenever any symbol is `near_expiry` or `proof_window_risk ==
"unknown"`, `None` only when `all_passed` itself has no truth-bearing
value), `proof_window_risk` (worst across symbols, ranked
high/unknown/medium/low), and `operator_action` (first non-empty per-symbol
message). Every one of the 5 pre-existing early-return response
constructions (`backend_unavailable` × 2, `no_evidence`, `parse_error` × 2)
sets the 3 new top-level fields to `None` — no change to their existing
truth_state/error semantics.

**Design decision (documented, not implemented as elapsed-time
adjustment):** the classifier operates only on the evidence's own
`latest_completed_bar_age_secs`/`max_allowed_age_secs` snapshot fields, not
an elapsed-time-since-`produced_at_utc` adjustment — matching the exact
headroom/overage numeric behavior specified for this patch (age 913/max 900
→ overage 13; age 850/max 900 → headroom 50, near_expiry; age 300/max 900 →
headroom 600, low risk). The `01A` audit's finding about evidence-snapshot
vs. live dispatch-tick age drift remains the documented rationale for why
Phase D's script-level `-MinFreshnessHeadroomSeconds` safety margin exists.

**Tests:** extended
`scenario_intraday_md_refresher_operator_surface_01.rs` with IRS-12
(overage → `staleness_overage_secs=13`, `risk=high`, `proof_window_ready=
false`), IRS-13 (headroom 50 within the 120s near-expiry threshold →
`near_expiry=true`, `risk=high`, `proof_window_ready=false` even though the
symbol itself still `passed=true`), IRS-14 (headroom 600 → `risk=low`,
`proof_window_ready=true`), IRS-15 (missing age/max fields →
`risk=unknown`, `operator_action` explains the gap, `proof_window_ready=
false` — fail-safe on missing evidence). All fixture-file-only, same
synthetic temp-dir pattern as IRS-01..11; no provider/DB/broker calls. 15/15
pass (11 pre-existing + 4 new).

**Validation:** `cargo check -p mqk-daemon` clean. `cargo test -p mqk-daemon
--test scenario_intraday_md_refresher_operator_surface_01`: 15/15 pass.
`cargo clippy -p mqk-daemon --lib -- -D warnings` clean (one doc-comment
lazy-continuation lint fixed during development). `git diff --check` clean.
`validate_intraday_provider_clock_skew_01a_audit.ps1` PASS (unaffected by
this phase's Rust-only changes).

**Phase C skipped:** the route-visible fields and their tests were added
directly in this phase (same files Phase C would have touched) —
`INTRADAY-PROVIDER-CLOCK-SKEW-01C-OPERATOR-STATUS-SURFACE-01` is a no-op per
the mission's own conditional-skip instruction.

### INTRADAY-PROVIDER-CLOCK-SKEW-01D-SMOKE-RUNNER-PREFLIGHT-GUARD-01 — CLOSED_LOCAL

**Mission:** teach `Start-PaperTradingSmoke.ps1 -RequireIntradayRefresh` to
reject (not just accept) evidence that is fresh but too close to its
freshness cap to survive startup + first dispatch tick — a script-preflight
guard only, never a daemon gate change.

**Built:** new `-MinFreshnessHeadroomSeconds` parameter (default `120`).
`STEP 14C` gained a new block, after the existing `truth_state`/
`stale_or_missing_evidence`/`all_passed` checks (all unchanged): it prefers
the `01B` route's `proof_window_ready`/`proof_window_risk` fields when
present (fails closed unless `proof_window_ready == true`, printing each
symbol's `latest_completed_bar_ts`/`latest_completed_bar_age_secs`/
`max_allowed_age_secs`/`freshness_headroom_secs`/`near_expiry`/
`proof_window_risk` via a new `Format-HeadroomSymbolDetail` helper); when an
older daemon build lacks those fields it falls back to a manual per-symbol
`freshness_headroom_secs < $MinFreshnessHeadroomSeconds` comparison instead
of silently skipping the check. Both failure paths print the same
